cpp.error: requires a pointer to a null-terminated character array

divergences.reason: Dart values have no C character-pointer representation, so %s deliberately uses toString().

cpp.result: implementation-permitted spelling of infinity and NaN

divergences.reason: Format chooses stable special-value spellings from the representations permitted by C++23.

cpp.result: depends on the active floating-point rounding mode

divergences.reason: Format has no process-global floating-point environment and always applies deterministic nearest-even rounding.

dart.result: symbols and digit alphabet supplied by NumberLocale

divergences.reason: format_intl and NumberLocale expose locale capabilities beyond the normative LC_ALL=C comparison.

cpp.result: wraps after an explicit conversion to an unsigned C type

divergences.reason: Unsigned printf conversions reject negative Dart integers instead of applying a hidden machine-width wrap.

cpp.error: undefined behavior for an invalid conversion specification

divergences.reason: Invalid percent grammar is rejected before argument access with structured format context.
Dart strings are Unicode and %c accepts a valid Unicode scalar rather than one narrow byte.
String width and precision use Unicode scalars by default, with grapheme clusters available explicitly.
The supported compatibility target is the selected C++23 sprintf subset, not later %b/%B additions.

cpp.result: conversion selected by a fixed-width length modifier

divergences.reason: Dart int and BigInt do not expose the C integer-width type matrix, so length modifiers are intentionally absent.
The core API accepts Dart values and does not expose native pointer formatting or %n writes.
Arguments are consumed sequentially; the non-standard POSIX dollar-index syntax is not part of the dialect.

cpp.error: requires selection of a finite-width integer type

divergences.reason: Supported Dart int and BigInt magnitudes are formatted directly rather than coerced to a machine width.
